daily_thesis: The August 20 backfill is not a fresh abstract-level deep dive; it is a source-audited recovery of the missing Thursday batch. Its strongest signal is that geometry, manipulation data, and world-model latents are being judged by whether they change a robot policy, route, or benchmark state. APRL should treat the day as a benchmark-design map: define the hidden state, material state, viewpoint state, or future latent that can falsify a deployment claim before scaling data collection.

clusters.cluster: Geometry becomes a policy-facing intervention instead of a reconstruction side product
clusters.why: The date-section titles connect geometry to frozen VLA viewpoint handling, field LiDAR navigation, dynamic 4D reconstruction, UAV SLAM, visual odometry, and LiDAR scene flow. That means the useful question is not whether the map looks plausible; it is whether viewpoint, metric scale, odometry, or dynamic-flow evidence changes a route, manipulation policy, or downstream failure.
clusters.confidence_note: Six 3D/Scene papers independently tie geometry to VLA policy use, field navigation, SLAM/VO evaluation, 4D reconstruction, or LiDAR flow.
clusters.lab_action: Compare frozen-VLA viewpoint canonicalization, monocular SLAM, visual-odometry matching, 4D Gaussian reconstruction, and LiDAR scene-flow cues on camera-shift, scale-drift, crop-row navigation, dynamic-object, and route-recovery splits; score action delta, localization failure, and downstream navigation success.

strategy_board.title: Policy-facing geometry stress suite
strategy_board.thesis: Test whether viewpoint canonicalization, metric SLAM, visual odometry, and field LiDAR cues change robot action robustness.
strategy_board.one_week: Create camera-shift and field-route episodes with GS map, SLAM/VO, and LiDAR navigation variants around the same policy.
strategy_board.four_week: Build a reusable route/manipulation suite that exports viewpoint error, scale drift, route recovery, and action deltas.
strategy_board.success: A geometry intervention predicts or prevents a policy failure that success-only metrics hide.
strategy_board.stop: Geometry variants do not change policy ranking or failure prediction under controlled camera and route shifts.
strategy_board.asset: Camera-shift videos, route traces, scale checks, LiDAR navigation logs, and action-delta labels.

strategy_board.title: Manipulation state-label benchmark
strategy_board.thesis: Separate deformability, lab-tool hierarchy, partial-view geometry, human video edit quality, and reward transition labels.
strategy_board.one_week: Annotate ten manipulation failures with material deformation, tool-subtask boundary, hidden local geometry, and recovery action labels.
strategy_board.four_week: Turn the labels into a small benchmark that compares human-video-derived experience, reward models, and partial-view grasping.
strategy_board.success: State labels explain a policy failure or recovery difference that final success does not.
strategy_board.stop: Labels collapse to the same ranking as final success or cannot be annotated reliably.
strategy_board.asset: Failure-state taxonomy, annotated clips, tactile/deformation notes, subtask hierarchy, and partial-view geometry labels.

strategy_board.title: Decision-aligned world-model probe
strategy_board.thesis: Evaluate whether future latents preserve the variable that changes a driving, navigation, or whole-body control decision.
strategy_board.one_week: Use three traffic or navigation scenes where one latent variable changes braking, route choice, or control recovery.
strategy_board.four_week: Compare decision-aligned latent objectives with video-quality or reconstruction objectives under matched scenarios.
strategy_board.success: Decision-aligned latents better predict action changes or near-miss avoidance than visual-quality scores.
strategy_board.stop: Latent alignment improves no downstream decision metric under controlled scenario edits.
strategy_board.asset: Edited scenarios, latent probes, decision deltas, near-miss labels, and control outcome traces.
